classification.difficultyReason: Combines equal-side triangle properties, supplementary angles and several adjoining angle sectors.

content.prompt:
Determine the size of the missing angles in each diagram.
You do not need to show working out.

spec.description: Horizontal-base triangle divided from its apex to the base midpoint. Single ticks on the left outer side, internal segment and both base segments. Six angle sectors.
spec.mathematics: The left subtriangle is equilateral; the right subtriangle is isosceles. All four marked segments are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Supporting original student figure image42.png has no numerical givens. All four single-ticked segments are equal and determine every missing angle. Numerical answers appear only in the solution.

answer.short: Left base: $60^\circ$; apex, left then right: $60^\circ$, $30^\circ$; internal base point, left then right: $60^\circ$, $120^\circ$; right base: $30^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The left triangle has three equal sides, so each angle is $60^\circ$.

At the internal base point, the angle sector on the right is supplementary to $60^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=180^\circ-60^\circ\\&=120^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
The right triangle has two equal sides, so its remaining two angles are equal:
$$\begin{aligned}2\phi+120^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\phi&=60^\circ\\\phi&=30^\circ.\end{aligned}$$

answer.short: Left base: $62^\circ$; apex, left then right: $62^\circ$, $28^\circ$; internal base point, left then right: $56^\circ$, $124^\circ$; right base: $28^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The given left apex angle is $62^\circ$. The equal sides in the left triangle give a left base angle of $62^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta+62^\circ+62^\circ&=180^\circ\\\theta&=56^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
The adjoining angle on the straight base is
$$\begin{aligned}\psi&=180^\circ-56^\circ\\&=124^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
The right triangle has two equal sides:
$$\begin{aligned}2\phi+124^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\phi&=56^\circ\\\phi&=28^\circ.\end{aligned}$$

spec.answerVisibility: Show only the original 74-degree given at the left base, angle D--A--B, evidenced by image45.png. Withhold every other numerical angle label from the question diagram.

answer.short: Left base: $74^\circ$; apex, left then right: $53^\circ$, $26.5^\circ$; internal base point, left then right: $53^\circ$, $127^\circ$; right base: $26.5^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Using the given left base angle of $74^\circ$, the other two angles of the left isosceles triangle are equal:
$$\begin{aligned}2\theta+74^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\theta&=106^\circ\\\theta&=53^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
The adjoining angle on the straight base is
$$\begin{aligned}\psi&=180^\circ-53^\circ\\&=127^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
The right triangle has two equal sides:
$$\begin{aligned}2\phi+127^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\phi&=53^\circ\\\phi&=26.5^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
Thus the source's $27^\circ$ labels are rounded values; its exact equal angles are $26.5^\circ$.

spec.description: Tilted triangle with upper-left, right and bottom vertices. Horizontal internal segment joins a point on the left side to the right vertex. Double ticks on the upper left-side segment, internal segment and lower right side. Full right vertex has a right-angle square.
spec.mathematics: Two adjoining isosceles triangles, supplementary sectors at the internal left point, and complementary sectors at the right vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: Show only the original 30-degree given in the upper-right sector, angle P--R--Q, evidenced by image48.png. Withhold every other numerical angle label. Retain all double-tick families and the full right-angle mark.

answer.short: Upper-left: $30^\circ$; internal point, upper then lower: $120^\circ$, $60^\circ$; right vertex, upper then lower: $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$; bottom: $60^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Let each equal angle in the upper triangle be $u$, and each equal angle opposite the marked equal sides in the lower triangle be $v$.

The upper triangle's third angle is $180^\circ-2u$. The two sectors at the internal point lie on a straight line:
$$\begin{aligned}(180^\circ-2u)+v&=180^\circ\\v&=2u.\end{aligned}$$
The lower triangle's angle at the right vertex is $180^\circ-2v$. The full angle at that vertex is $90^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned}u+(180^\circ-2v)&=90^\circ\\2v-u&=90^\circ\\4u-u&=90^\circ\\3u&=90^\circ\\u&=30^\circ\\v&=60^\circ.\end{aligned}$$
The upper angle at the internal point is $120^\circ$; the lower angle at the right vertex is $60^\circ$.
